title: Shortness of Breath Triage Protocol
body: Dyspnea assessment: Determine onset (acute vs chronic/progressive), severity (at rest vs exertional), position dependency (orthopnea), associated symptoms (chest pain, cough, fever, leg swelling, wheezing). Ask about known asthma, COPD, heart failure, or recent immobilization/surgery (PE risk). Assess ability to speak in full sentences. Red flags: inability to speak in sentences, cyanosis, tripod positioning, stridor, acute onset at rest, associated chest pain, or history suggesting PE/anaphylaxis.
disposition_notes: Severe dyspnea at rest or inability to speak → ER_NOW. Acute onset with fever/cough → URGENT_CARE. Mild exertional dyspnea, chronic and stable → SAME_DAY or ROUTINE.
